# Independent ICC matrix-shaper fixtures

`DisplayP3-v4.icc` and `AdobeCompat-v2.icc` come from
[`saucecontrol/Compact-ICC-Profiles`](https://github.com/saucecontrol/Compact-ICC-Profiles/tree/bdd84663061bc4ae95ca70decff54f581e27f702)
at revision `bdd84663061bc4ae95ca70decff54f581e27f702`, in its `profiles/`
directory. Its [CC0 license](LICENSE-CC0) is included. The Display P3 file
uses the standard sRGB transfer curve. The Rust test feeds their exact bytes
to moxcms; the LittleCMS oracle reopens those same serialized files.

The additional `display-p3-gamma22.icc` and `adobe-rgb-1998.icc` ICC v4
profiles are generated by LittleCMS 2.19 from D65 Display P3 primaries with
gamma 2.2 and Adobe RGB (1998) primaries with gamma 2.19921875. These exercise
a second profile serialization and transfer-curve variant. The generator and
the independent linear-sRGB oracle are in [tools/generate.c](tools/generate.c).

From the repository root on a machine with LittleCMS headers and library:

```sh
cc -O2 tests/fixtures/icc/tools/generate.c -o /tmp/ferrisma-icc-oracle $(pkg-config --cflags --libs lcms2)
/tmp/ferrisma-icc-oracle
shasum -a 256 tests/fixtures/icc/*.icc
```

The generator reopens all four serialized ICC files before requesting oracle
values. It uses floating-point RGB input and output, a linear-sRGB
destination, relative colorimetric intent, no black-point compensation, and
`cmsFLAGS_NOCACHE`. Samples include primaries, mixed colors, neutrals, and U8
codes 10 and 11 around the sRGB transfer knee. The test embeds its printed
sample values. No native CMS is
linked into the engine or required to run the Rust tests. The ICC header date
is pinned to 2026-11-10 so regeneration is byte-for-byte deterministic.

| Profile | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `DisplayP3-v4.icc` | `cb51de38e482ee974c0c76b9689e16aad04bad16e226fed2f30c842d15ff3a3d` |
| `AdobeCompat-v2.icc` | `60fb2adecacf82132db0b1c09b303316f3bbd9e2823e7ba096d01627d12d57c9` |
| `adobe-rgb-1998.icc` | `b7701708dd23c22c20ad22833a641ffcb2b76cea8be465c181f312f599f011a0` |
| `display-p3-gamma22.icc` | `1f54ab299e0561e59cf105bd1de2e34ebf64986c63cfd42718f72b4606580fe7` |

This covers four RGB matrix-shaper profiles and selected U8 samples, including
colors outside sRGB. It does not establish equivalence for arbitrary ICC LUTs,
rendering intents, real photographs, or HDR content.

The observed maximum absolute differences from LittleCMS 2.19 on this sample
set were:

| Profile | In-gamut pixels | Out-of-gamut pixels | Knee pixels |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `DisplayP3-v4.icc` | `9.96e-5` | `5.93e-4` | `1.12e-6` |
| `AdobeCompat-v2.icc` | `4.58e-7` | `6.54e-4` | `4.58e-7` |
| `display-p3-gamma22.icc` | `1.10e-4` | `5.93e-4` | not asserted |
| `adobe-rgb-1998.icc` | `0` | `6.54e-4` | not asserted |

## Real photograph (issue #17, 2026-11-12)

`tests/icc_photo.rs` uses the libavif test photograph
`codecs/libavif-rs/upstream/libavif/tests/data/paris_exif_xmp_icc.jpg`
(403 x 302, SHA-256
`a827613b7d2b44b62547a83452d5399f2f42d96b88738032a5fde933cf31263c`; see that
directory's README for its source and license). Its embedded profile is a
596-byte Google sRGB IEC61966-2.1 ICC v4 profile.

```sh
J=codecs/libavif-rs/upstream/libavif/tests/data/paris_exif_xmp_icc.jpg
magick "$J" icc:tests/fixtures/icc/paris-srgb.icc
magick "$J" -crop 96x64+150+100 +repage -depth 8 rgb:tests/fixtures/icc/paris-crop.rgb
cc -O2 tests/fixtures/icc/tools/photo.c -o /tmp/ferrisma-icc-photo $(pkg-config --cflags --libs lcms2)
/tmp/ferrisma-icc-photo
```

ImageMagick 7.1.2-35 decodes the JPEG with its own libjpeg-turbo, so the
crop's samples are independent of the workspace decoder. `tools/photo.c`
converts the crop with LittleCMS 2.19 (same settings as `generate.c`) once
through the photo's own profile and once through `DisplayP3-v4.icc`, which
gives real photographic content a wide-gamut meaning.

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `paris-srgb.icc` | `33c34ecfeb998459e0075ba26a0f1ea5042e20e2419c5962e495eba3208576f2` |
| `paris-crop.rgb` | `eacf9a7468e8d0ac8c5bce44213ab2a14eb61c1898188b4b71e3a5d0cb896578` |
| `paris-crop-srgb-icc.f32` | `2baf73706a5d3c96f276b4f8c302443e5c4b67a10a1b5ee23440d4340d4598c2` |
| `paris-crop-as-p3.f32` | `3961758cf3985d5532e9a42debede411254bec04889300da2798d33d1b204800` |

The engine output (JPEG adapter or lossless WebP with an `ICCP` chunk,
rendered-ICC policy, identity geometry) must lie, per sample, between the
sRGB8 encodings of the LittleCMS value plus and minus `8e-4` linear (the
bound below). All 18,432 samples of each case do; 103 LittleCMS samples of
the P3 case lie outside `[0, 1]`. This is one photograph and two
matrix-shaper profiles, not a corpus, and no LUT-based profile or rendering
intent other than relative colorimetric is covered.

## Tolerances of the profile samples

The tests allow `8e-4` linear on the selected general samples, above the
measured `6.54e-4` maximum. They allow only `1e-5` on the real-profile knee
samples, where a zero result or a gamma-only curve differs from the oracle by
roughly `0.002` to `0.003`. A pixel is listed as out of gamut when any oracle
channel falls outside `[0, 1]`, including tiny white-point roundoff.
